claims.text: The starting material is a nanoscale HEA multilayer coating containing FCC and BCC phases.
Progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading is governed by interactions between dislocation dynamics and severe lattice distortion.
Interactions between dislocations and lattice distortion produce unusual deformation behavior in HEA multilayers.
The proposed dislocation–lattice-distortion interaction enhances strain hardening.
The proposed dislocation–lattice-distortion interaction improves deformation tolerance.
Dislocation density and spatial distribution are the structural mediators of the deformation response.
The operative mechanism is dislocation glide coupled to interactions with lattice distortions.
The coating will be subjected to sustained uniaxial tensile loading at 500 MPa and room temperature.
The strain-hardening exponent will increase by 20% relative to the stated starting baseline.
Deformation tolerance will improve by 15% relative to the stated starting baseline.
The comparison baseline is a conventional metallic multilayer with similar composition and structure.
The proposed hypothesis is bounded to nanoscale multilayer coatings with a minimum thickness of 100 nm.
The exact contribution of short-range order to the deformation response is uncertain.
The effects of grain-boundary interactions on dislocation dynamics are uncertain.
An observed strain-hardening-exponent increase below 10% relative to baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
A reduction in deformation tolerance exceeding 5% would falsify the hypothesis.
